title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotype-reinforcing versus stereotype-challenging responses in ambiguous and disambiguous question-answering contexts related to religion, using the BBQ dataset. It also evaluated the agent's ability to follow a rule of not claiming to have religious beliefs.
findings: The reinforcement learning (RL) finetuning process used to create the Sparrow model amplified stereotype-reinforcing biases related to religion compared to the baseline Dialogue-Prompted Chinchilla (DPC) model. On the BBQ benchmark for ambiguous questions, the bias score for religion increased from 0.07 (DPC) to 0.12 (RL), and for disambiguous questions, it increased from 0.05 (DPC) to 0.07 (RL).
